CleanupRun.description: What a task's cleanup runs: of the same kind as the task (see PROJECT.md, Per-task cleanup).

oneOf.description:
The function given to `@task(cleanup=...)`, found with the task's when the runner
imports the DAG file.
A command, with the task's environment.

A script of the task's script root (`[jobs.<name>.cleanup]`), with the task's
environment and working directory.

args.description: Its arguments, each one argument (never a shell string).

interpreter.description: The interpreter: an `[interpreters]` entry of the worker that runs it.

script.description: The script, relative to the script root.

oneOf.description: A string run by a shell; it takes no references (decision 99): values go in `env`.
A program and its arguments, run without a shell; each element is one argument.

DagCtxField.description: A field of the run's context, `dag_ctx.run.*` and `dag_ctx.dag_id`.

oneOf.description: `dag_ctx.run.id`.
`dag_ctx.run.kind`.
`dag_ctx.run.planned_for`.
`dag_ctx.run.since`.
`dag_ctx.dag_id`.
`dag_ctx.event.key`.
`dag_ctx.event.data`.
`dag_ctx.event.at`.

DagLocation.description: Where a DAG is defined: a DAG root and a file path relative to it.

path.description: The file's path relative to the root, with `/` separators.

root.description: The root's name (see PROJECT.md, DAG roots).

Edge.description: A dependency: `to` runs after `from`, when `from` ended with one of the outcomes `on`.

on.description:
The upstream outcomes the edge is taken on (`.on(...)`); empty for any outcome. An edge
not taken counts as skipped in the downstream task's trigger rule.

EdgeKind.description: Why one task depends on another.

oneOf.description: The downstream task takes the upstream task's output (or a part of it).
An order-only dependency (`>>`), no data passed.
From a `@branch` task: taken when the branch chose the downstream task.
From a resource's setup to a user (`uses=`): it can stop the user, never make it run.

Encoding.description: How a reference's text is written into its template.

oneOf.description:
Percent-encoded, every byte but RFC 3986's unreserved ones (`A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~`):
a value in a URL (a typed connection's) is only the text it stands for, never the
URL's structure (another host, a query).

Expand.description: What a mapped task's instances vary over (decision 69): one instance per element.

oneOf.description:
`.expand(name=values, ...)`: each argument a list (a literal or a reference to a list),
in the order written; the instances are their cartesian product, the first argument
varying slowest (decision 79).
`.expand_kwargs(values)`: a list of dicts, each one instance's arguments.

Field.description: A named field of a `TypedDict` or dataclass.

required.description: Whether the field must be present (`TypedDict`) or has no default (dataclass).

Group.description:
A group of tasks (`with group("load"):`): a name for some of a DAG's tasks, drawn as a box
around them in the UI. It has no state and no rule of its own (decision 56A).

id.description: The group's ID, unique within its DAG (`load`, `load.eu` for a nested one).

parent.description: The group it is nested in, if any.

Mapped.description: One mapped argument of `.expand(...)`: its name and the list it maps over.

value.description: Its list: a literal, or a reference to a list.

OutcomeDecl.description: One of a task's outcomes: its name, and for a `command` task the exit code meaning it.

exit_code.description: A `command` task's exit code for it; none for other tasks.

name.description: The name (an `Outcome` enum member's, a class's, or `None`).

Params.description: The run parameters a DAG takes (`Dag(params=SomeDataclass)`, decision 138).

defaults.description:
The fields' defaults, as JSON: the values of a scheduled run, and of the fields a
trigger leaves out.

schema.description:
A JSON Schema of the class, as JSON values (a date as `format: date`): what the master
checks a trigger's values against, and what the UI's form is built from.

type.description:
The declared class's type: a dataclass or a Pydantic model. Values are stored by it,
as outputs are (tagged).

anyOf.description: A dataclass field or dictionary key.

PathElem.description: One step of a path into an output: a field or key, or a list / tuple index.

Reference.description: A reference to data known only at run time.

oneOf.description: An upstream task's output, or a part of it.

on.description:
The outcomes it was narrowed to (`.on(...)`); empty for any. On another outcome,
or a skipped upstream task, it stands for `null`.

path.description: The path into the output; empty for the whole output.

oneOf.description: An upstream task's outcome itself (`.outcome`), as its name.
A field of the run's context.
The run's parameters, or a part of them (`dag_ctx.params.region`, decision 138).

path.description: The path into the parameters; empty for all of them.

oneOf.description:
A secret from a secret storage (`secrets['etl/db']['password']`), fetched by the agent
that runs the task, never by the master (see PROJECT.md, Secret storage).

default.description:
What a reference reads when the secret or its key is missing
(`secrets['etl/db'].get('password', '')`); a key's only, never declared in `secrets=`.

key.description:
The key in the secret (`password`); none for the whole secret, an object of key to
value.

path.description: The secret's path in the storage (`etl/db`).

storage.description: The storage it comes from; none for the default one.

Resource.description: A resource: one thing of two parts, each a task of the DAG, both always there (decision 259).

blocking.description:
Whether what follows its group waits for its cleanup (decision 266); the edges from
the cleanup say so, this is for showing them (decision 272).

cleanup.description: The task that undoes it, once every user is done.

setup.description: The task that creates it; its ID is the resource's.

unschedulable_timeout_ms.description:
How long a user may stay `unschedulable` before it fails, so the cleanup can run
(decision 273); none: no limit.

ResourceRole.description: A command's or a script's part in a resource, for `schedr task-ctx resource set|get`.

oneOf.description:
A `CommandResource`'s or `ScriptResource`'s setup: its output is the value it reports with `resource set`,
of the task's `output_type` (`none`: it reports nothing), not its `ProcessResult`.

A resource's `cleanup_command` or `cleanup_script`: it reads the setup's value with
`resource get`.

RunIf.description:
A task's trigger rule: what its upstream edges must have done for it to run (see
PROJECT.md, Outcomes, failures and joins). An edge not taken counts as skipped.

oneOf.description:
Every edge that wasn't skipped succeeded, and at least one did: skipped when all were
skipped, `upstream_failed` when one failed.

Every edge succeeded: `upstream_failed` when one failed, otherwise skipped when one
was skipped.

RunOf.description: Which run of another DAG a step waits for, and of it which task (decision 353).

lag_ms.description:
With it, the run whose `planned_for` is the waiting run's minus this many milliseconds;
without it, the next run to end after the step starts.

SecretDecl.description:
A secret a task declares in `secrets=`: one it may read on demand (`schedr task-ctx
secret get`, `task_ctx.secret(...)`), fetched before its process starts, or a prefix
covering every secret under it, fetched when read.

oneOf.description: One secret, or a whole one (every key).

default.description:
What a reference reads when the secret or its key is missing
(`secrets['etl/db'].get('password', '')`); a key's only, never declared in `secrets=`.

key.description:
The key in the secret (`password`); none for the whole secret, an object of key to
value.

path.description: The secret's path in the storage (`etl/db`).

storage.description: The storage it comes from; none for the default one.

oneOf.description: Every secret under a prefix (`SecretPrefix('connections/')`), at any depth.

storage.description: The storage; none for the default one.

oneOf.description: `@sensor`: its function does the waiting.
`@sensor.poke`: its function is called every `every_ms`.

SensorWaitFor.description:
What an `@sensor(wait_for=RunOf(...))` waits for, and the parameter its function is given the
run in (its first: a `RunResult`).

param.description: The function's parameter given the run.

run_of.description: The run, and of it which task.

timeout_ms.description:
`@sensor(wait_for=..., timeout=...)`: how long one call may take, in milliseconds; one
over it fails the attempt (its retries get the same run). `None`: what is left of
`max_wait`.

oneOf.description: A `@task` function, found by task ID when the runner imports the DAG file.

branch.description:
A `@branch` task: its output is the list of the downstream task IDs it chose, and
its outgoing edges are selection edges.

oneOf.description:
A wait step (`@sensor`, `@sensor.poke`): found by task ID, as a `Python` task, and ending
with its value or with the `TimedOut` outcome.

every_ms.description: How often to call it (`Poke`), in milliseconds.

max_wait_ms.description: How long it waits, in milliseconds; `None`: the worker's `[sensors] default_max_wait`.

wait_for.description:
`@sensor(wait_for=RunOf(...))` (decision 353): called once a matching run of another
DAG has ended, with it as `param`, rather than at once.

oneOf.description:
`first_of` / `at_least` (decision 347): ended by the master, no process and no slot, as
soon as enough of its upstream edges are taken. Its output is `{"$value": ..., "winner":
...}`: the winner's output and ID, or for `at_least` lists of them in the order they ended.

`wait_for(RunOf(...))` (decision 353): waits for a run of another DAG, or one of its
tasks, ended by the master with no process and no slot. Its value is that run's ID; it
ends `Failed` when the run (or task) ended otherwise, and `TimedOut` after `max_wait`.

max_wait_ms.description: How long it waits, in milliseconds; `None`: the master's `[sensors] default_max_wait`.

oneOf.description: An inline command, run by the agent.

connection_env.description:
Connections given as variables and files (decision 184:
`connections={"DB": warehouse}`), by prefix: `DB_URL`, `DB_PGPASSFILE`, ... Each
is also in the task's `connections`.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the process.

resource.description:
Its part in a resource (M4.8d): a `CommandResource`'s setup, or a resource's
`cleanup_command`; `None` for any other command.

oneOf.description:
A script declared in a `schedr.toml` (M4.9): run by the agent with the declared
interpreter, from its script root at the version the master expects. A standalone job's
task.

args.description: Its arguments, each one argument (never a shell string).

env.description: Extra environment variables for the process.

interpreter.description: The interpreter: an `[interpreters]` entry of the worker that runs it.

job.description: The declaration: `<root>:<schedr.toml's path in the root>#<name>`.

resource.description: Its part in a resource (`ScriptResource`, `cleanup_script`), if any.

script.description: The script, relative to the script root.

working_dir.description: Where it runs, relative to the script root (`schedr.toml`'s directory by default).

oneOf.description: An `EmptyOperator`: completed by the master, no process.

cleanup.description: Its cleanup, if it has one.

connections.description:
The connections it opens (`connections=`, decision 179), by name: only these, opened
before it starts.

expand.description:
What its instances vary over, for a mapped task (`.expand(...)`); its `arguments` are
then the fixed ones (`.partial(...)`).

group.description: The group it belongs to (the innermost), if any (decision 64).

id.description: The task's ID, unique within its DAG.

outcomes.description: The outcomes it may end with (see PROJECT.md, Task results and outcomes).

output_type.description: The type of its output (`process_result` for commands, `none` for empty tasks).

secrets.description: The secrets it declares (`secrets=`): read on demand, never put in its environment.

TaskCleanup.description: A task's cleanup: `finally` for each of its attempts (see PROJECT.md, Per-task cleanup).

anywhere.description: Whether it may run on another worker when its own is lost (`cleanup_anywhere`).

handles.description:
The handle types it takes: `None` any, none listed none (a function without a `handles`
parameter would never see them).

retries.description: How many times it is retried after a failed try, on the same worker.

retry_delay_ms.description: The delay before each retry, in milliseconds.

timeout_ms.description: How long one try may run, in milliseconds; `None`: `[worker] cleanup_timeout`.

TaskSettings.description: A task's settings, resolved from its own arguments and the defaults that apply to it.

fresh_process.description:
A Python task: always a new process, never forked (for code that misbehaves after a
fork). Not for other tasks.

max_active.description:
At most this many of its instances running at once, across all runs (decided from
the DAG's current version, decision 87A); `None` for no limit.

max_active_per_run.description:
At most this many of its instances running at once within one run (from the run's own
version); `None` for no limit.

max_output_size.description: The output size limit in bytes.

preload.description:
A Python task: fork it from the preloaded fork server (`false`: only from the bare
one, for code that misbehaves next to the preloaded libraries). Not for other tasks.

queue.description: The queue the task goes to.

retries.description: How many times a failed attempt is retried.

retry_delay_ms.description: The delay before each retry, in milliseconds.

run_if.description: When it runs, from its upstream edges (its trigger rule).

timeout_ms.description: The attempt's timeout in milliseconds; `None` for no timeout.

Template.description: A t-string as data: its parts in order.

TemplatePart.description: One part of a template: literal text, or a reference filled in at run time.

oneOf.description: Literal text.
A reference, rendered at run time.

TemplateRef.description: A reference inside a template, with its optional format spec (e.g. `%Y-%m-%d`).

oneOf.description: An upstream task's output, or a part of it.

on.description:
The outcomes it was narrowed to (`.on(...)`); empty for any. On another outcome,
or a skipped upstream task, it stands for `null`.

path.description: The path into the output; empty for the whole output.

oneOf.description: An upstream task's outcome itself (`.outcome`), as its name.
A field of the run's context.
The run's parameters, or a part of them (`dag_ctx.params.region`, decision 138).

path.description: The path into the parameters; empty for all of them.

oneOf.description:
A secret from a secret storage (`secrets['etl/db']['password']`), fetched by the agent
that runs the task, never by the master (see PROJECT.md, Secret storage).

default.description:
What a reference reads when the secret or its key is missing
(`secrets['etl/db'].get('password', '')`); a key's only, never declared in `secrets=`.

key.description:
The key in the secret (`password`); none for the whole secret, an object of key to
value.

path.description: The secret's path in the storage (`etl/db`).

storage.description: The storage it comes from; none for the default one.

encode.description: How the text is written into the template, if not as it is (decision 188).

format.description: The t-string format spec, if any.

Trigger.description: What starts runs of a DAG besides people (and other DAGs).

oneOf.description: Nothing: manual runs only.
A cron expression (5 or 6 fields, or a preset such as `@daily`) evaluated in a time zone.

catchup.description:
Whether missed fire times get runs in order (`true`) or only the most recent
(`false`).

end.description: The last run it creates is for the last fire time at or before it.

start.description:
The first run it creates is for the first fire time at or after it; without it,
the moment the master first stored the DAG.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone name, e.g. `Europe/Warsaw`; `UTC` by default in the Python API.

oneOf.description: A fixed interval measured in real time (UTC), unaffected by daylight saving.

catchup.description:
Whether missed fire times get runs in order (`true`) or only the most recent
(`false`).

end.description: The last run it creates is for the last fire time at or before it.

interval_ms.description:
The interval in milliseconds; fire times are whole intervals from `start`, or from
the Unix epoch without one.

start.description:
The first run it creates is for the first fire time at or after it; without it,
the moment the master first stored the DAG.

oneOf.description: A single fire time (it has no previous fire time).

A `@trigger` function, which runs in a worker's watcher host and yields events: each new
one starts a run.

restart_if_idle_ms.description: Started again from its bookmark when no event came for this long; `None`: never.

run_retries.description:
`@trigger(wait_for=RunOf(...), run_retries=N)` (decision 353): a run its function
raised on is tried again this many times, then passed, recorded; `None`: tried until
`schedr triggers skip` passes it.

start.description: It runs from this moment on.

task.description:
Its function as a task of kind `sensor`: its literal arguments, whether it is called
every so often, its queue, its secrets and connections. It isn't in the graph.

oneOf.description:
`trigger=RunOf(...)` (decision 353): a run per run of another DAG (or its task) that
succeeded while this one is live, planned for that run's `planned_for` plus `lag`, or for
the moment the master saw it.

TypeDesc.description: The type of a value that can be stored as a task output.

oneOf.description: Anything (an explicit `Any`): only the run-time check applies.
`None`.
`bool`.
`int`.
`float`.
`str`.
`datetime` (stored tagged).
`date` (stored tagged).
`timedelta` (stored tagged).
`list[T]`.
`tuple[A, B, ...]` (stored tagged).
`dict[str, T]` (keys are always strings).
`Literal[...]`.

values.description: The allowed values (strings, integers, booleans or `null`).

oneOf.description: A union, including `Optional[T]` (`T | None`).
A `TypedDict`.
A dataclass.

name.description: The class name, for messages and outcome names.

oneOf.description:
A Pydantic model (decision 59), described by Pydantic's JSON Schema of it: what
`model_dump(mode="json")` writes. Only the Python layer compares it; here its parts
are `Any`.

name.description: The class name, for messages and outcome names.

oneOf.description: The output of a `command` or `script` task.

Value.description:
A task argument: a literal, a reference, a template, or a container of values (so
references inside lists and dictionaries stay visible).

oneOf.description:
A JSON value as encoded by the Python API (with tagged extra types such as
`{"$datetime": "..."}`), passed as is.
A reference, passed with its type (a `date` stays a `date`).
A t-string, rendered to a string.
A list whose elements may contain references.
A dictionary (string keys) whose values may contain references.

description: A DAG: its identity, trigger, tasks and dependencies.

description.description: A description shown in the UI.

groups.description: The task groups (decision 64), for the UI and the API; the master schedules tasks only.

initial_since.description: `since` of the run on the DAG's first fire time (see PROJECT.md, Runs).

max_active_runs.description: At most this many runs at a time; `None` for no limit.

max_active_tasks.description:
At most this many of its tasks running at once, across all its runs (each instance of
a mapped task counts); `None` for no limit.

params.description: The run parameters it takes (`Dag(params=...)`); none: it takes none.

produced_by.description: The schedr version whose runner produced this JSON.

tags.description: Tags shown in the UI and used for filtering.

trigger.description: What starts its runs (besides people and other DAGs).
